source_text: Ne quantum a praeceptis, tantum ab auribus dei longe simus, memoria praeceptorum uiam orationibus sternit ad , caelum; quorum praecipuum est, ne prius ascendamus ad altare dei, quam, si quid discordiae uel offensae cum fratribus contraxerimus, resoluamus. quale est enim ad pacem dei accedere sine pace? ad remissionem debitorum cum retentione? . quomodo placabit patrem iratus in fratrem, cum omnis ira ab initio interdicta sit nobis? nam et Ioseph dimittens fratres suos ad perducendum patrem, et ne, inquit, irascamini in uia. nos scilicet monuit — alias enim uia cognominatur disciplina nostra — tum ne in uia orationis constituti ad patrem cum ira incedamus. exinde aperte dominus amplians legem iram in fratrem homicidio superponit. ne uerbo quidem malo permittit expungi: etiam si irascendum est, non ultra solis receptum, ut apostolus admonet. quam autem temerarium est aut diem sine oratione transigere, dum cessas fratri satisfacere, aut orationem perseuerante iracundia perdere?
thought_title: Peace with brothers before approaching God
orientation: Tertullian is explaining the first and chief precept of prayer: before going up to God's altar, a Christian must resolve any discord or offense with fellow believers.
pass_a_gloss: Lest we be as far from the ears of God as we are from the precepts, the memory of the precepts paves a way for prayers to heaven; of which the chief one is, that we should not go up to the altar of God before we resolve whatever discord or offense we have contracted with brothers. For what kind of thing is it to approach the peace of God without peace? To approach the remission of debts with retention? How will an angry man placate the Father, angry at his brother, since all anger has been forbidden to us from the beginning? For Joseph also, sending away his brothers to bring back their father, said, 'And do not be angry on the way.' He warned us, of course—for our teaching is called 'the way' elsewhere—then, lest we, placed on the way of prayer, should go to the Father with anger. From then on the Lord, openly amplifying the law, places anger against a brother above homicide. He does not permit it to be discharged even by an evil word: even if one must be angry, not beyond the setting of the sun, as the apostle admonishes. But how rash it is either to pass a day without prayer while you delay satisfying your brother, or to lose your prayer while anger persists?

choices.english: paves a way for prayers to heaven
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of road-building, which connects to the later 'way of prayer' and the quotation from Joseph about not being angry 'on the way'.
rejected: opens a path for prayers to heaven
prepares a road for prayers toward heaven

choices.english: to the remission of debts with retention
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'debts' for debita and keeps the stark contrast between remission and retention, which is the rhetorical point.
rejected: to the forgiveness of debts while holding on to them
to the pardon of debts with withholding

choices.english: places anger against a brother above homicide
choices.why: Renders superponit literally as 'places above' to preserve the surprising claim that anger is ranked above homicide in the Lord's amplification of the law.
rejected: puts anger on the same level as homicide

choices.term: ne uerbo quidem malo permittit expungi
choices.english: does not permit it to be discharged even by an evil word
choices.why: Expungi means to be wiped out or discharged; keeping 'discharged' preserves the sense that anger is not allowed even a small outlet.
rejected: does not allow it to be vented even by an evil word
does not permit it to be satisfied even by an evil word

choices.english: not beyond the setting of the sun
choices.why: Receptum solis is the sun's withdrawal or setting; this literal rendering matches the temporal limit Paul gives for anger.
rejected: not past the going down of the sun

choices.english: while you delay satisfying your brother
choices.why: Satisfacere means to make amends or satisfy; 'satisfying' keeps the legal and relational force of making things right with a brother.
rejected: while you put off making amends to your brother
while you hesitate to reconcile with your brother

pass_b_english: So that we may not be as far from God's ears as we are from the precepts, the memory of the precepts paves a way for prayers to heaven. The chief of them is this: we must not go up to God's altar before we have resolved any discord or offense we have contracted with our brothers. For what kind of thing is it to approach the peace of God without peace? To approach the remission of debts with retention? How will a man placate the Father while he is angry at his brother, when all anger has been forbidden to us from the beginning? For Joseph, sending his brothers away to bring back their father, said, "Do not be angry on the way" (Genesis 45:24). He was certainly warning us—for our teaching is called by another name, the Way—not to walk toward the Father in anger while we are set on the way of prayer. From that point on the Lord, amplifying the law, places anger against a brother above homicide. He does not permit it to be discharged even by an evil word. Even if one must be angry, it is not to go beyond the setting of the sun, as the apostle admonishes (Ephesians 4:26). How reckless it is either to pass a day without prayer while you delay satisfying your brother, or to lose your prayer by persisting in anger!
